rationale: Using the worst recent cash-conversion realization rather than a level or mean is a substantively different (downside-floor) conditioner within a heavily mined cash-yield family, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis and sign, though the marginal information over the archived MA/level versions is likely small.

This is a cosmetic level→TREND swap on the archived "Cost-Scaled Cash Conversion EBITDA Yield," and the archive already demonstrates that this exact transformation destroys performance (Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount fmb 3.24 vs. Improving-Operations Cash Discount fmb 0.77).

Mechanically the same debt-funded-payout mechanism as the archived "Debt-Funded Payout Trap" with only the leverage measure narrowed from GROWTH(lt) to GROWTH(dlc/lt), and it fails to address that archived signal's diagnostic problem (correct-signed FMB slope but a large positive, sign-contradicting FF5 alpha), so the same conflict should be expected.

oancf/cogs is algebraically just (oancf/revt)÷(cogs/revt), i.e., a simplified restatement of the two components already combined in the archived "Operating-Quality Backed Cash Discount," so it is a near-rediscovery with less information content.

The expression is internally consistent (rising cost intensity plus falling cash conversion yields a high conditioner, interacted with high sales yield, negative expected sign) and the two-sided deterioration score is a genuine extension of the archived one-sided sales trap, though the reliance on 3-period TRENDs is a known weak transform in this archive.

This is a permutation of two archived signals — swapping the dp subtraction in "Maintenance-Covered Earnings Yield" for the dvc subtraction of "After-Payout Liability Cover Yield" and the denominator from lt to (act+lct) — so it is an incremental scaling variant rather than a new economic mechanism.
